title: Arkret Typed Realm Current Result
description: Closed domain result selected without protocol typed current result IDs. Every result names the last authority commit that affected the typed target.

realm_authority_root_value.description: Closed value of the lifetime-stable Realm authority root. Every member is derived by the registered ak.realm.create value_projection from the signed envelope and create payload; an author-supplied member is a realm_authority_root_conflict, never an accepted write.

controller_actor_id.description: Current root controller. At genesis it is exactly the create envelope actor_id.

controller_epoch.description: Increments only on a root controller rotation. Genesis is 0.

authority_generation.description: Increments only on a planned governance Station handoff. Genesis is 0.

realm_authority_root_result.description: Singleton authority-root typed current result. The selector carries no component beyond its kind, so (realm_id, selector) is the Realm's lifetime-stable authority root identity.

selector.description: Per-Realm singleton. encoding.md section 9.5.1 forbids restating the envelope realm_id in a subject, so the subject carries nothing beyond its kind.

realm_policy_result.description: Registered projection of the Realm policy reference. conformance/schema-registry.md fixes ak.realm.policy as a closed reference to one independently defined Policy object (payload.value.policy_id), so the family carries that reference and not the Policy document body: no projection kind can dereference a policy_id, and inline Realm facets live in ak.realm.policy_bundle or their dedicated facet Event kinds.

member_state_current.description: Closed value of the member_state typed current result: the materialized membership register of one complete ActorId. models/common-fields.md section 4.5 fixes it as a four-state register over join/knock/leave/ban. It is a named def rather than an inline object because registry/contract-registry.json cites it as the value_schema_ref of ak.member.state; an enclosing _result envelope names the selector and revision beside the value, so citing the envelope would let a value_projection member be checked against the wrong object.

selector.description: Section 9.8 keys the set per target: the subject is the reacted-to object, and the payload carries no other target field. v1 core additionally requires an ak:message: target in the same effective scope (section 9.8.2), which a reducer enforces on admission; profiles MAY register further reactable kinds, so the wire type stays the generic object_ref of reaction_payload.

message_reactions_result.description: Registered projection of one reaction target. models/strand-and-message.md section 9.8.3 is authoritative and says this family is the core keyed-set projection of authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9: ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove each project exactly one keyed_set_add, so a remove is itself an asserted element rather than an explicit revocation. The (target_ref, key, members[], count) summary of that section is the default view folded above this set, never the stored value.

message_reactions_current.description: Closed value of the message_reactions typed current result: the canonically sorted dot set of reaction assertions on one target. The join is the core keyed-set union, which stays commutative, associative and idempotent; remove-wins convergence is a default-view fold above it and MUST NOT be implemented as a sixth state model. The set keeps both sides of a concurrent (add, remove) pair because section 9.8.3 requires the audit view to rebuild them.

reaction_assertion_entry.description: One asserted element of the message_reactions keyed set. The tag is the canonical dot of the accepted Event write that produced it; the value is the complete reaction payload of that Event. The asserting actor and the polarity -- whether this is an add or a remove -- are deliberately NOT element fields: section 9.8.3 reads both from the signed envelope of the Event the dot names, because event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 forbids a projection from assembling, renaming or trimming fields.

canonical_event_dot.description: Stable tag of one registered reducer write: the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot of zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. A bare event_id is never a valid tag.

agent_key_authorization_entry.description: One tagged entry of the agent_key typed current result. The tag is the canonical dot of the accepted Event write that produced it; the value is the complete authorize or revoke payload of that Event.

agent_key_result.description: Registered reducer projection of one Agent signing key. It is the single state source a portable state witness may quote; a service-private key table is not an alternative.

selector.description: Composite subject derived from (agent_id, agent_key_id). Producers MUST NOT spell it by string concatenation.

agent_status_result.description: Registered Agent lifecycle projection. The first active value has exactly one provenance: the delegated PCR genesis ak.realm.create conditional write of zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1.

agent_key_current.description: Closed value of the agent_key typed current result.

authorizations.description: Canonically sorted active tagged-set entries. A revoke entry is a witnessed revocation boundary marker, never an active authorization.

realm_genesis_result.description: Singleton create-locked identity/security core. Written once by the registered ak.realm.create result write (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1); the value is the closed ak.schema.realm_genesis.v1 object.

realm_history_access_result.description: Singleton Realm history-access FSM current state (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1). Initialized by the conditional ak.realm.create write and moved only by ak.realm.history_access.

identity_resolution_result.description: Singleton Realm identity-resolution projection. The PCR reducer initialises it from the genesis object's initial_resolution on the conditional ak.realm.create write and ak.identity.resolution.update is its only post-genesis writer (zh/identity/identity-did.md section 4.2). The stored value is the five-member resolution_projection, not the three-member commitment the owner signs: resolution_event_ref and updated_at are reducer-derived from the carrying envelope and are read back off this result by section 5.

identity_accountability_result.description: One accountability endorsement (family identity_accountability). zh/models/actor.md section 3.3.1: there is one record with two writers, and its identity is (Realm, issuer principal, subject principal, normalized exact scope set) -- the Realm component is the scope this result lives in, so it is not a selector member. A grant that changes a provision endorsement MUST be written into the original controller PCR; the same tuple in another Realm is a different record and cannot revoke this one.

selector.description: Composite subject. Producers MUST NOT spell it by string concatenation; the registered composite derives its third component as string_set_digest(accountability_scope, ak.accountability_scope_set.v1), so the scope set carried here is the normalized set that digest is taken over.

capability_grant_result.description: Registered projection of one Capability Grant. The subject GrantId is derived by retyping the accepted ak.capability.grant Event id; the value is the complete projected grant, including reducer-inserted id and the registered derived members authority_depth / authority_root_refs (zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10).

call_recording_id_component.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript segment handle, canonical byte-for-byte (crypto-media/call-state.md section 5.1).

call_recording_state_current.description: Capture permission state of one recording segment: ak.call.recording.start opens it as recording, a committed ak.call.state recording_transition.to=stopped closes it. ready/failed artifact details live in the separate call_recording_artifact family.

call_transcript_state_current.description: Capture permission state of one transcript segment: ak.call.recording.start opens it as transcribing, a committed ak.call.state transcript_transition.to=stopped closes it.

call_state_result.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state state_transition axis (crypto-media/call-state.md section 4.1).

call_focus_result.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state focus axis. The first committed session_focus is binding (MEDIA-2); later writes MUST restate it verbatim.

call_recording_state_result.description: Capture permission state typed current result of one recording segment (family call_recording_state), keyed by the (call_id, recording_id) segment key so several captures in one call never collide.

call_recording_artifact_result.description: Published artifact typed current result of one recording segment (family call_recording_artifact): the ready/failed details published from stopped, referencing the exact confirmed stop Event. It grants no capture, key or read authority.

call_transcript_state_result.description: Capture permission state typed current result of one transcript segment (family call_transcript_state), keyed by the (call_id, recording_id) segment key.

call_transcript_artifact_result.description: Published artifact typed current result of one transcript segment (family call_transcript_artifact): the ready/failed details published from stopped, referencing the exact confirmed stop Event.

call_moderation_result.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state moderation_delta axis (crypto-media/call-state.md section 4.1).

call_roster_result.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state roster_delta axis. The current value is the last accepted write on the stream; per-participant durable identity is (call_id, actor_id, device_id).

call_mute_override_result.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state mute_override axis (crypto-media/call-state.md section 4.1).

call_summary_result.description: Write-once durable end-of-call summary (crypto-media/call-state.md section 7), written by ak.call.summary after the call reaches a terminal state.

strand_position_value.description: The registered value shape of strand_position, pinned by models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6 as list_space_id with rank, or null. The null branch is the pre-placement state of a Strand that has been created but never moved onto a Board.

realm_schema_result.description: Per-Realm declaration of the Realm-scoped Morph kind tightening (models/governance-objects.md section 4). Singleton: the Realm is given by the Event envelope, which conformance/encoding.md section 9.5.1 forbids repeating in the subject.

realm_link_result.description: One directed Realm-to-Realm link. models/realm-links.md section 5 makes the subject the (target_realm_id, link_kind) tuple with the source Realm given by Event scope, and the current value the last accepted write.

realm_join_rule_result.description: The Realm default_join_rule enum. models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3 makes ak.realm.join_rule its sole canonical carrier.

realm_alias_result.description: The Realm alias declaration or its tombstone. discovery/discovery-directory.md section 12 resolves an alias from this family and treats a tombstone as absent, so the tombstone branch is retained rather than collapsed to null.

realm_policy_bundle_result.description: The Realm policy components that have no facet Event kind of their own. models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3 restates the whole bundle on every policy_revision.

realm_asset_privacy_policy_result.description: The Realm asset metadata and download policy (crypto-media/media-and-blob.md section 12). It is deliberately not a policy_bundle component and is excluded from key_access_revision.

realm_plaintext_visible_services_result.description: The declared set of services that may see plaintext in this Realm (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3).

realm_media_service_result.description: The single settled media service binding of the Realm. crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 4 calls it a single-valued commit-ordered projection; section 2.1 pins the closed field set.

realm_read_receipt_policy_result.description: The Realm read receipt disclosure requirement (discovery/read-receipts.md section 2.5). Strand-level separation goes through a Circle, not through a second subject on this family.

realm_inheritance_policy_result.description: What this Realm inherits from one parent Realm. extensions/mimi-interop.md section 9.1 makes inheritance per-parent, and payload.source_realm_id is the parent carrier.

realm_tombstone_result.description: The terminal tombstone of the Realm, with its required successor_realm_id (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.6). Commit-ordered and written at most once.

realm_destroy_result.description: The terminal destroy of the Realm, which MUST NOT carry a successor (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.6). Commit-ordered and written at most once.

realm_set_default_strand_value.description: The registered value shape of realm_set_default_strand. models/strand-and-message.md section 2 makes the authoritative current value the Realm projection field default_strand_id and normalizes absent and explicit null to one null before a whole-value comparison, so the value is the one-member object carrying that field rather than a bare pointer: only a member can be absent.

realm_set_default_strand_result.description: The authoritative default_strand_id pointer of the Realm (models/strand-and-message.md section 1). The current value is the last accepted write on the stream.

strand_position_result.description: The position of one Strand on one Board. models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6 pins the subject to the reversible typed_pair of board_space_id and strand_id and forbids a hash subject, so both typed-ID components MUST be validated on parse.
